Hi Grace,

Hope you're well. We switched a feature to production earlier than planned on Jun 2 and saw a sharp increase in token consumption. Our June invoice shows a one-time overage of ~$12,400 that we weren't prepared for. I attached the usage export and our invoice for reference.

We value Redwood and want to continue scaling, but this kind of unexpected charge is a problem for our procurement and finance teams. Two asks:
- Can Redwood review the usage and confirm the spike was legitimate (we're including the feature rollout notes)?
- If validated, can we work out a one-time credit or amortized settlement to avoid disrupting our renewal conversation next month?

We're open to a compromise (partial credit + commitment to a stepped capacity increase) if that helps. We have a renewal coming up July 15 and would prefer to resolve this without pausing the contract.

Folks — forwarding NovaCorp's note. Quick context: they launched a preview to 100% traffic on Jun 2 (we saw a steep token distribution shift). They're asking for a one-time credit or an amortized settlement and want this clarified before their renewal on Jul 15.

My initial read: spike looks genuine (feature rollout), but it's a strategic customer and expansion opportunity. Options I think we should consider:
- Offer 40% credit on the overage and bill the remainder as a one-off invoice
- Or apply 60% toward their next invoice as a credit and convert them to a stepped committed capacity (3-month ramp) with a 10% uplift in committed tokens at a discounted rate

Ben — can you run the usage verification + confirm any billing system constraints for mid-cycle credits? Laura — I'll need an approved credit amount to present and a short note for procurement.

Thanks,
Grace

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-06-21T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected Jun invoice spike — request to reconcile

Grace / Laura,

I pulled NovaCorp's token logs and invoice reconciliation. Summary:
- Jun 2–18: sustained 6.5x baseline token rate coincident with the rollout timestamp.
- No evidence of duplicated requests or obvious telemetry anomalies on our side; calls match legitimate service endpoints.
- Calculated overage = $12,389.26 (matches their invoice line).

Billing constraints: we can issue a one-time credit in July (post-close) or apply credit to their next invoice. We can also split a credit: part now, part applied to renewal.

Recommendation (balanced commercial + risk):
1) Offer a one-time credit equal to 35% of the overage (~$4,336).
2) Apply 50% of the remaining balance (~$3,026) as a credit toward their first post-renewal invoice if they sign the 12-month stepped commit by Jul 15 (commit details below).
3) Require a brief MOU (email thread suffices) acknowledging the settlement and commit start date.

Proposed commit: 12-month term, quarterly capacity steps (Q3 +15%, Q4 +25%, Q1 +40%), 8% volume discount on committed token consumption. That should cover their expected growth and gives them predictable unit pricing.

If Finance approves the 35% one-time credit, I can generate the credit memo and Laura can add the extension to the renewal paperwork.

-ben

Attachments: [analysis_notes_NovaJun.pdf] (internal)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Unexpected Jun invoice spike — request to reconcile

Hi Elena — thanks for sending the usage and invoice. We verified the consumption and confirmed the spike aligns with your Jun 2 rollout.

Proposal to close this quickly and keep your July renewal on track:
- Redwood will issue a one-time credit equal to 35% of the Jun overage (credit memo for $4,336).
- We will apply an additional credit equal to 50% of the remaining overage balance to your first post-renewal invoice, conditional on signing a 12-month stepped committed capacity by Jul 15. The applied credit would be ~$3,026.
- Commit details: 12 months, quarterly capacity steps (Q3 +15%, Q4 +25%, Q1 +40%), with an 8% discount on committed token spend.

Next steps:
1) If this works, reply to confirm and Laura will add the settlement language to the renewal doc.
2) Ben and Finance will issue the one-time credit memo the week after renewal closes (timing depends on billing cycle).

We believe this split approach balances their unexpected cost with predictable pricing going forward and helps NovaCorp scale without a billing surprise at renewal. If you prefer a different split (larger one-time credit, smaller commit), we're open to a brief follow-up call.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
